## LeBron James — Short Biography

**LeBron Raymone James** (born December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, U.S.) is an American professional basketball player nicknamed **"King James."** Standing 6 ft 9 in (2.06 m) and playing small forward / power forward, he currently plays for the **Philadelphia 76ers** (No. 23) in the NBA, after previous stints with the Cleveland Cavaliers (2003–2010, 2014–2018), Miami Heat (2010–2014), and Los Angeles Lakers (2018–2025).

Born and raised in Akron, James gained national attention at **St. Vincent–St. Mary High School**, where he was heavily touted as a future NBA superstar. He was the **#1 overall pick in the 2003 NBA Draft** by the Cleveland Cavaliers, won Rookie of the Year, and quickly established himself as one of the league's best players.

**Career Highlights:**
- 🏆 **4× NBA Champion** (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020) — including ending Cleveland's 52-year championship drought in 2016
- 🏅 **4× NBA Finals MVP**
- 🥇 **4× NBA MVP** (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013)
- ⭐ **22× NBA All-Star** (record) and 3× All-Star Game MVP
- 📊 **NBA's all-time leading scorer**
- 🥇 **3× Olympic gold medals** with the U.S. national team (and 2024 Olympics MVP)
- 🛡️ **NBA Rookie of the Year** (2004)
- 13× All-NBA First Team selection (record) and 6× All-Defensive Team

The oldest active player in the NBA, he holds records for the most seasons played (23), most games played, most field goals made, and ranks 4th in NBA career assists and 6th in career steals. He is widely considered one of the greatest athletes in history, and by many, the greatest basketball player of all time.

Sources: Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James), biography.com, and Britannica.
